title: A domain is only the beginning.
description: Certificates, routing and history. Build the relationship, then try to break it.

steps.title: Expand the public names
steps.action: Search the authorized domain in certificate records. Retain certificate identity, fingerprint and observation dates.
steps.trap: A certificate name does not prove current control or reachability.
steps.fallback: Compare a second certificate view; label missing observations, not missing assets.

steps.title: Add infrastructure context
steps.action: Inspect existing routing and service records for candidate infrastructure. Record each source observation time.
steps.trap: Shared hosting and CDNs make IP co-location weak attribution evidence.
steps.fallback: Use official organization documentation when provider coverage is absent.

steps.title: Reconstruct the timeline
steps.action: Compare dated captures around a public infrastructure or branding change. Keep capture and publication times separate.
steps.trap: Archive absence is not proof of nonexistence. A historical relationship may have ended.
steps.fallback: Try the other archive and record the coverage gap.

steps.title: Challenge the attribution
steps.action: Compare existing scan records with the domain owner's own public documentation. Separate observed links from ownership claims.
steps.trap: A shared resource can be a vendor, template or analytics service, not common ownership.
steps.fallback: Keep the result as an unconfirmed lead; request scoped active validation separately.

title: Follow the company, not the name.
description: Resolve stable identifiers before connecting filings, parents and procurement.

steps.title: Resolve the legal identity
steps.action: Match the legal entity using registration number, jurisdiction and LEI where available.
steps.trap: Similar trading names can identify unrelated companies.
steps.fallback: Use the original national registry and record the unresolved identity.

steps.title: Inspect relationship evidence
steps.action: Read the original parent relationship record or dated filing and identify what kind of relationship it actually states.
steps.trap: Reporting exceptions are not concealed ownership; filings can contain issuer errors.
steps.fallback: Record the exception and compare the latest amended filing.

steps.title: Trace public procurement
steps.action: Search the resolved identifier and legal-name variants. Separate notices, awards and modifications.
steps.trap: A tender announcement is not a completed contract.
steps.fallback: Find the original procurement notice and its corrections.

steps.title: Screen and corroborate
steps.action: Treat matches as candidates; check underlying records, dates and exact identifiers.
steps.trap: Inclusion in an aggregator or a name match does not establish wrongdoing.
steps.fallback: Retain the ambiguity and seek manual review; never merge people or entities by name alone.

title: Find what the page used to say.
description: Compare two independent crawl histories, then preserve what you can actually prove.

steps.title: Bound the change
steps.action: Choose captures on either side of the alleged change. Note gaps and exact source URLs.
steps.trap: The first available capture is not necessarily first publication.
steps.fallback: Expand the time range without silently changing the hypothesis.

steps.title: Check another collection
steps.action: Find matching URLs in a separate crawl index and compare timestamps and content digests.
steps.trap: A different digest may reflect dynamic content rather than the claim of interest.
steps.fallback: Inspect the relevant content rather than relying on digest inequality alone.

steps.title: Preserve and report
steps.action: Capture accessible pages when authorized, hash exported artifacts and preserve the observation and uncertainty separately.
steps.output: A replayable archive and evidence receipt
steps.trap: A receipt proves a local hash at a claimed time, not third-party authenticity.
steps.fallback: Preserve the original archive reference when recapture is unavailable.

title: A picture. Several competing stories.
description: Combine local metadata, public map geometry and solar constraints without inventing certainty.

steps.title: Preserve before interpreting
steps.action: Hash the original locally. Inspect metadata on a copy and list only visible, non-sensitive clues.
steps.trap: Editable metadata cannot authenticate a scene by itself.
steps.fallback: State that metadata is absent; continue with visible features.

steps.title: Intersect scene constraints
steps.action: Bound a region and compare roads, waterways and public landmarks. Keep multiple candidates.
steps.trap: Overpass and OpenStreetMap share data; they are not independent corroboration.
steps.fallback: Use additional official imagery or first-party location records.

steps.title: Try to disprove the time
steps.action: Test candidate orientation and solar position over the claimed date interval. Record assumptions.
steps.trap: A matching shadow does not prove a unique time or place.
steps.fallback: Report the unresolved geometry; do not force a single location.

title: A hotspot is a clue. Not a cause.
description: Separate sensor observations, geographic context and independent reporting.

steps.title: Read the observation
steps.action: Inspect detections for the bounded area and time. Retain sensor, resolution and observation timestamp.
steps.trap: Thermal anomalies can have several causes and can be missed.
steps.fallback: Expand the sensor/time comparison and disclose the gap.

steps.title: Check geographic context
steps.action: Compare public geographic features and known industrial or natural context without identifying private people.
steps.trap: Current map features may postdate the event.
steps.fallback: Seek dated official geographic records.

steps.title: Find independent reporting
steps.action: Look for original local reporting and official statements, not repeated syndicated copies.
steps.trap: Many articles may repeat one claim. Reports do not substitute for the sensor limitations.
steps.fallback: Keep the cause unknown when primary corroboration is absent.

title: Trace the model behind the model.
description: Read the claims, pin the revision and connect public code without executing artifacts.

steps.title: Pin the declared provenance
steps.action: Record the model repository, revision, card, declared base model and dataset references.
steps.trap: A model card is not proof of the actual training set.
steps.fallback: Explicitly mark undocumented components as unknown.

steps.title: Resolve the linked code
steps.action: Read linked public repositories at specific commits. Compare license and evaluation references.
steps.trap: Names and copied README files do not establish authorship or provenance.
steps.fallback: Prefer publisher-signed references or documented release records.

steps.title: Check package context
steps.action: Resolve relevant package ecosystem and versions and read upstream advisories. Do not load weights or run repository code.
steps.output: A scoped dependency and advisory note
steps.trap: Dependency metadata is not a proof that an advisory is reachable in the model service.
steps.fallback: Report declared dependencies separately from observed runtime components.

title: A package name is not an identity.
description: Resolve the ecosystem, verify the repository, then read the actual advisory.

steps.title: Resolve package and version
steps.action: Record the ecosystem, exact package version and linked project before following dependencies.
steps.trap: The same name can exist in several registries; a dependency graph is environment-dependent.
steps.fallback: Use the original registry and project release metadata.

steps.title: Match the public source
steps.action: Compare version, tag, commit and publisher links without executing the code.
steps.trap: A repository URL in package metadata is a claim that can be wrong.
steps.fallback: Leave unverified provenance as unresolved.

steps.title: Read affected ranges
steps.action: Inspect published affected versions and original advisory references. Separate package exposure from exploitability.
steps.trap: An affected version alone does not establish runtime impact.
steps.fallback: Request a separate authorized environment review.

title: Outage, blocking, or a local failure?
description: Compare genuinely different collection vantage points instead of counting dashboards.

steps.title: Inspect existing measurements
steps.action: Compare timestamps, networks, test outcomes and control behavior from existing measurements.
steps.trap: An anomalous result is not automatically deliberate blocking.
steps.fallback: Report sparse coverage instead of running unsolicited measurements.

steps.title: Compare network signals
steps.action: Align traffic observations and routing changes to the same UTC interval.
steps.trap: Aggregated visibility can conceal a local failure or overstate a regional effect.
steps.fallback: Narrow the hypothesis to the actually observed networks.

steps.title: Seek first-party context
steps.action: Locate original operator notices and independent reporting. Preserve conflicting explanations.
steps.trap: A traffic drop alone does not identify intent or a responsible actor.
steps.fallback: Keep intent unknown and state the observable impact only.

title: Follow the DOI, not the headline.
description: Resolve the publication, inspect the authors' claims and separate metadata from evidence.

steps.title: Resolve the original work
steps.action: Find the DOI, publisher and publication metadata. Check the original work and any corrections.
steps.trap: A DOI identifies a work, not its correctness.
steps.fallback: Resolve the publisher record directly.

steps.title: Map the research context
steps.action: Inspect cited works and institution identifiers. Verify ambiguous author matches.
steps.trap: Citation volume does not establish validity; aggregation can misresolve identities.
steps.fallback: Use the original paper and author-provided identifiers.

steps.title: Crosswalk identifiers
steps.action: Use referenced identifiers to bridge records, then follow citations back to the primary source.
steps.trap: An unsourced graph edge is not an independent confirmation.
steps.fallback: Leave the crosswalk unresolved rather than merging by display name.

title: Ten headlines. How many sources?
description: Find the original observation underneath the repetition.

steps.title: Collect a bounded corpus
steps.action: Find reporting in a date window and preserve original article URLs, bylines and cited evidence.
steps.trap: Language coverage and indexing are uneven.
steps.fallback: Record what the query could not cover.

steps.title: Recover earlier claims
steps.action: Inspect earlier captures and follow quoted references to their first accessible source.
steps.trap: Earliest found does not mean first ever published.
steps.fallback: Use a qualified first-observed date.

steps.title: Preserve the dependency graph
steps.action: Group syndicated copies, copied statements and genuinely independent observations before writing a conclusion.
steps.output: A report distinguishing repetition from corroboration
steps.trap: Different publishers can rely on the same upstream witness or press release.
steps.fallback: Treat a single-origin claim as uncorroborated.
